author: JulianneSTR
quote:
- Extremely high price
- Scummy ultimate edition that cuts content from the game
- Promotes all digital future (ew).
- Runs like absolute crap.
- Pause menu is the worst in the series and it's made to sell you microtransactions.
- Music is heavily inferior to previous entries.
- MORALE SYSTEM IN A GAME ABOUT BEING A BAD PERSON. 
- Excessive realism mechanic wise like if anyone asked for Rockstar to not let us have the classic weapon wheel.

Gameplay wise, the devs clearly wanted to make a red dead auto. It doesn't work. It just does not feel like GTA. I don't want a random invisible meter to change the way the game develops, it has no place in this franchise. There has always been a tacit pact between player and game in GTA: The game allowed the player to be the most free individual ever in the sandbox, but said player accepted the story as it is, and understood the crazy things done in the sandbox might or might not have actual correlation with the story. This game, however, breaks that pact, since it wants you to live the sandbox the way they intended and not the way you want. Sure, you can just say "**** it" and play it like any GTA, but then the game will make sure you feel like **** for doing so. The gameplay also limits your immediate access to weapons heavily, like RDR2, and does not allow you full freedom to shoot in many places you'd want. To finish this off, it's clear that GTA VI is constantly fighting with it's own nature as a GTA, and you feel it while playing because the game does not respect that tacit pact I have described before. Instead, it tries to enforce it's view of Jason and Lucía in the way that you play with them in the sandbox, and if you don't follow that path, you'll get punished by the game system. GTA did not need more consequences for being an ****, as such consequences already existed and they go from one to six stars.
Music wise it's just inferior to all main entries since GTA III, it's not horrendous but it really can't compare to GTA V or IV.

The price is extremely high, with cut content from the base game being packed inside an "ultimate edition" yet they have the balls to put a **** STORE in the pause menu. Disgusting. All that WHILE selling you an empty physical box with NO DISC, so you can't refund, share the game with any friends, or own the product at all.
Moreover, after so many years in development, and behind such a high price, you'd expect the game to run accordingly. No, it doesn't. It not only doesn't run at 60 which is the standard, but it also doesn't run at stable 30 FPS. Rockstar tries to justify this by saying the PS5 is "too weak" instead of admitting their lazyness or doing their job. We can have debates about if the PS5 could or could not run it at 60 with a performance mode, but not being able to reach stable 30 is objectively pathetic and a scam.

It's a shame, because the game behind all this crap is good. If it wasn't because of it's fundamental contradictions with the nature of the franchise GTA (Which would be as simple as not to call it GTA VI), the horrendous anti-customer practices, and the atrocious performance, it'd probably deserve a high score. If you, dear reader, are curious on why I chose a 0 instead a 5-7 of a score (which would be more faithful to the game's content), it's mostly because of how this game tries to boycott the rights of it's customers and make them think it's okay.

My recommendation? Don't give Rockstar your money. The game is good but it's not worth it's price. It's basically a tech demo with bad writing and various simulations for you to go through. This product attempts against customers, their rights, and their intelligence.
